title: Condition evidence
audience: Home-based property managers who record the condition of properties at intake, during tenancy and at handover
learningOutcomes: Record condition evidence that separates pre-existing damage from damage caused during a tenancy or job.
Capture dated, referenced photographs and notes at intake and before handover.
Respect privacy when photographing occupied properties.

instruction.heading: Separate existing condition from new damage
instruction.body: Condition evidence protects the owner, the manager and the occupant. At intake, record the condition of each room and fixed item with dated, referenced photographs taken from the same positions each time. Note existing marks, chips, stains and wear. When a dispute arises later, the question is what was there before. Without an intake record, a scratch on a floor can be blamed on anyone. Keep the evidence with the asset register so that the condition history of each item is visible.

instruction.heading: Photograph with care
instruction.body: Photograph the property, not the occupants' private items. Take photographs with the occupant's consent where they are present, and avoid photographing personal papers, mail, medication or children. Keep photographs stored securely and share them only with the owner and people who need them. A photograph taken from a marked position at each inspection makes change easy to see. A condition note that says what was seen, where and when is as useful as a photograph. Taking condition photographs during an inspection means entering the home, so the entry rules below apply. In New South Wales, an inspection needs a minimum of seven days' notice given in writing, and no more than four inspections may take place in any twelve-month period (page last modified 24 May 2024). Entry is generally barred on Sundays and public holidays, and before 8am or after 8pm (page last modified 1 October 2026). In Victoria, a general inspection needs seven days' notice, may not be made in the first three months of the agreement, and can happen no more than once every six months (page last updated 24 April 2025). In Queensland, a routine inspection needs at least seven days' notice on the entry notice form and can happen no more than once every three months (no page date shown).

procedure: Record the condition of each room and fixed item at intake, with dated photographs from marked positions.
Note existing marks, chips, stains and wear in writing.
Repeat the same photographs at each inspection and before handover.
Photograph only the property, and avoid personal items and people unless consent is given.
Store photographs securely and share them only with the people who need them.
Compare the handover condition with the intake record and note any change.

workedExamples.situation: At handover, a floor shows a scratch near the door. The intake record does not show a scratch in that position.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the change be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Compare the handover photographs with the intake photographs from the same position. If the scratch is new, record it as a change since intake, with the date and position. Do not assume who caused it. Share the comparison with the owner and keep the evidence on file.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera or phone with date stamp

commonErrors.error: Taking photographs from different positions each time.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark the positions at intake and repeat them.

commonErrors.error: Photographing personal items or people without consent.
commonErrors.prevention: Photograph the property only, and get consent where people are present.

commonErrors.error: Assuming who caused a change without evidence.
commonErrors.prevention: Record what changed, where and when, and leave the cause open.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Confirm them before any photograph is stored or shared.

The notice and frequency figures above are minimum rules as shown on the cited pages. They are a checking aid, not legal advice. The tenancy agreement and the state regulator decide the position for a specific tenancy.
Completing this lesson does not give a licence or authority to make decisions on tenancy, bonds or disputes.

qualityStandard: Intake condition is recorded with dated photographs from marked positions.
Handover is compared with intake, and each change is recorded as a change with its position and date.
Photographs of people or personal items are taken only with consent.
documentationEvidence: Intake condition record with dated photographs from marked positions
Handover comparison record listing any change
Consent record for any photograph that includes people
summary: Record intake condition with dated photographs from marked positions.
Separate existing condition from change, and leave the cause open where no evidence exists.
Photograph the property with consent, and store the evidence securely.

knowledgeChecks.question: At handover a new scratch is found on a floor. What is the correct record?
options: Assume the last tenant caused it, since the scratch was not there before the move in the house
Compare with the intake photographs from the same position, and record the change with date and position
Delete the intake photographs, since they are no longer needed for the file or the property record
Ignore it because it is small and nobody else will notice the mark at all in the flat today

knowledgeChecks.question: When is it appropriate to photograph people at a property?
options: Never, in any case at all

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say intake photographs should be taken?
options: Only of the furniture, without dates
At random angles to show the room
Dated, referenced, and from the same positions each time
